subject: Article 8 Citizen Participation Mechanisms
overview: The Article 8 Subcommittee reviewed and revised draft charter provisions governing citizen participation mechanisms, including free petitions, citizen initiative measures, referenda, and recall procedures. The subcommittee refined specific signature thresholds and timelines across each section to present to the full Charter Study Committee.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The subcommittee approved the minutes of the March 13 meeting.

items.title: Free Petitions
items.summary: Members agreed to focus draft language on group petitions requiring 50 signatures to trigger a hearing, debated language preventing duplicate content within a year, and discussed hearing timeframes for the City Council and School Committee.

items.title: Citizen Initiative Measures
items.summary: The subcommittee established preliminary thresholds of 250 initial signatures with at least 25 per ward, followed by a requirement of 10 percent of registered voters gathered within 90 days, and discussed subsequent supplemental petition rules.

items.title: Citizen Referendum Procedures
items.summary: Members reviewed provisions for challenging newly passed measures, tentatively settling on a 12 percent registered voter signature threshold to protest or suspend an ordinance.

items.title: Recall Provisions
items.summary: The subcommittee agreed to remove any requirement to state grounds for recall, settled on an initial threshold of 500 signatures for citywide officials and 300 for ward officials, a subsequent 20 percent registered voter petition threshold, and minimum turnout requirements for recall elections.

items.title: Public Engagement and Future Agenda
items.summary: The subcommittee discussed proposals by Browne to strengthen public engagement mandates, agreeing to consult the Collins Center and consider incorporating broad engagement principles into the charter preamble.
